title: StrictRoosDerivation
statement: Let C be a site, small in a common universe containing its object, morphism and coefficient universes, and R a sheaf of commutative rings. Assume abelian sheafification and the locally-bijective characterization of its equivalences. Let A=Mod(R) [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], assume exact countable products, and fix derived categories of A and Tow(A) in a common localization universe [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let F be the explicit strict Roos functor, ι_X:lim X_n→F(X) its canonical zero-first-coordinate inclusion [def-weil-strict-roos-model], and u its one-minus-transition endomorphism [def-weil-tower-transition-endomorphism]. There exist a functor CF:D(Tow(A))→D(A) and a natural isomorphism κ:F⋙Q_A≅Q_Tow⋙CF such that the unit ν_X=Q_A(ι_X)κ_X makes CF a total right derived functor of ordinary termwise tower limit followed by Q_A, relative to quasi-isomorphisms. Moreover ι_I is a quasi-isomorphism for every K-injective complex I of towers whose degree terms I^p are injective objects of Tow(A).

source.place: Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok, proof and strict naturality refinement

proof.text: The explicit product functor takes quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms because countable products are exact. Apply the mapping-cone triangle and two-out-of-three, then shift, to show roosF preserves quasi-isomorphisms. Localize roosF followed by Q to obtain CF and the natural factorization κ.

Construct the kernel universal property of the ordinary-limit inclusion into the product using adjacent compatibility and induction. Transport the product and kernel to every degree and compute the signed differential of the shifted cone. Apply roosComplex_quasiIso to this data; its coordinate equation identifies its canonical map with roosι. Thus roosι is a quasi-isomorphism for every K-injective tower.

Module sheaves are Grothendieck abelian. For a small diagram category, evaluation left adjoints applied to a separator form a separating family; their coproduct is a separator, and filtered colimits are exact pointwise. Lift the natural-number index category to the module universe and transport back along its equivalence. Apply functorial K-injective resolutions in this Grothendieck tower category.

Prove the left Kan universal property directly. For β:G→Q E, a resolution q:X→T X and ν:G→F invertible on resolutions, define the component F(q) ν(T X)^{-1} β(T X) E(Qq)^{-1}. Naturality follows from q, ν and β. Fully faithful whiskering along Q descends this transformation to CF→E; its factorization follows from ν and β naturality. Uniqueness holds on resolved objects by cancellation of ν and κ, then on every object by naturality along Qq. Use ν=Q(roosι), whose resolution components are invertible by the preceding step.

lean.statement:
theorem strictRoosDerivation
    {C : Type uC} [Category.{vC} C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C)
    [HasSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{max uC vC r}]
    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{max uC vC r}]
    (R : Sheaf J RingCat.{max uC vC r})
    (_hcomm : ∀ (U : Cᵒᵖ) (a b : R.obj.obj U), a * b = b * a)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ringedSiteModules.{max uC vC r} R)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w}
      (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ringedSiteModules.{max uC vC r} R)]
    [HasExactLimitsOfShape (Discrete ℕ) (ringedSiteModules.{max uC vC r} R)]
    : ∃ (CF : DerivedCategory.{w} (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ringedSiteModules.{max uC vC r} R) ⥤
        DerivedCategory.{w} (ringedSiteModules.{max uC vC r} R))
      (κ : roosF ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q.{w} ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.{w} ⋙ CF),
      CF.IsRightDerivedFunctor (roosDerivedUnit κ)
        (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ringedSiteModules.{max uC vC r} R)
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) ∧
      ∀ (I : CochainComplex (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ringedSiteModules.{max uC vC r} R) ℤ)
        [I.IsKInjective] (_hIinj : ∀ p : ℤ, Injective (I.X p)), QuasiIso (roosι I)
